triggers.grounds: Retro-scan lexical false positive: the matched phrase 'the sentence zone's own strategy bound closes at web:Eccl.7.14' carries no translation-punctuation fact. 'Sentence zone' here names the book's own sentence-literature stretch at 7:1-14, a genre zone argued from Hebrew form, not WEB sentence structure, quotation-mark layout, paragraph layer or poetry lines; no tier-4 layout fact is cited anywhere in the row, whose only WEB material is a verbatim rendering quote at web:Eccl.7.15. Both seams rest on tier-1 bytes standing in the cited verses' own text: the front edge on the perfect רָאִ֖יתִי (oshb:Eccl.7.15, byte tier) against the imperatives הֱיֵ֣ה and רְאֵ֑ה of oshb:Eccl.7.14 (byte tier), the rear edge on the negative imperative אַל תְּהִ֤י (oshb:Eccl.7.16, byte tier). No tier-4 fact does driver or corroboration work here, so the trigger is not_a_defect. The same clause is a register violation on an unrelated ground and is recorded as a separate finding.

findings.claim: The row's first cross-seam disclosure quotes רָעָ֖ה as 'the raah root of oshb:Eccl.7.14's own closing imperative', but that run is the resh-ayin noun ('adversity'); the raah-root imperative in that verse is רְאֵ֑ה.
findings.grounds: MT 7:14 carries both runs consecutively and both collate at BYTE tier at oshb:Eccl.7.14: רָעָ֖ה ('adversity', resh-ayin) followed immediately by the imperative רְאֵ֑ה ('consider', raah). device_notes item (1) attaches the raah-root label and the 'closing imperative' description to רָעָ֖ה; item (2) of the very same field then attaches רָעָ֖ה to the resh-ayin root ('two distinct objects on the same root, not blended') -- one byte run labelled two different roots inside one field. The neighbour row at web:Eccl.7.13-Eccl.7.14 argues the identical cross-seam tie with the correct token ('the raah root of its own closing imperative, רְאֵ֑ה'), so the two rows describe one seam with incompatible tokens. Byte-valid splice, semantically the wrong word for the claim. Not load-bearing: the seam itself stands on the perfect רָאִ֖יתִי (oshb:Eccl.7.15, byte tier) against the imperative register of 7:13-7:14, which the row also states.
findings.proposed_change: device_notes item (1): replace the splice רָעָ֖ה with רְאֵ֑ה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier). No dependent edit follows -- item (2) already carries רָעָ֖ה under the resh-ayin root, and the seam warrant is unchanged.

findings.claim: device_notes item (3) says this verse's 'paradox nouns' both recur in the next span, but only the first recurs as a noun; at oshb:Eccl.7.17 what recurs is the consonantal root inside a verb.
findings.grounds: צַדִּיק֙ spliced from oshb:Eccl.7.15 collates at BYTE tier at oshb:Eccl.7.16 -- a true noun recurrence, correctly cited. רָשָׁ֔ע spliced from oshb:Eccl.7.15 collates at oshb:Eccl.7.17 only at SKELETON tier: that verse's own byte run is the second-person verb תִּרְשַׁ֥ע (byte tier at oshb:Eccl.7.17), not the noun. The sentence carries one 'byte tier' label and the single object word 'nouns' for both members, blending a byte-level noun recurrence with a skeleton-level root-in-verb recurrence, against the book's name-the-object-then-count rule. Texture disclosure only; no seam rests on it.
findings.proposed_change: Split the claim by object and tier: keep צַדִּיק֙ (oshb:Eccl.7.15 -> oshb:Eccl.7.16, byte tier) as the noun recurrence, and re-label the second member as the resh-shin-ayin root recurring in the verb תִּרְשַׁ֥ע (byte tier at oshb:Eccl.7.17; skeleton tier against this verse's own רָשָׁ֔ע).

findings.claim: Two register-purge violations in row prose: a citation of the governing strategy document in boundary_rationale, and a positional row reference in device_notes.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'the sentence zone's own strategy bound closes at web:Eccl.7.14' -- a strategy-document citation inside row prose, which the register purge bars alongside decision-ids, file-order talk and tool filenames; the audited row at web:Eccl.7.19 states the same zone fact without it ('that zone's own bound at web:Eccl.7.14'), so a compliant formulation already exists in the corpus. device_notes reads 'recur in the following row's own span at oshb:Eccl.7.16 ... and oshb:Eccl.7.17' -- a positional row reference where the verses are already named, so it carries nothing the verse anchors do not. Both are cosmetic: no evidence claim in the row depends on either, and the underlying facts re-derive true.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale: drop the document reference -- 'the sentence-literature zone closes at web:Eccl.7.14'. device_notes: replace 'in the following row's own span at' with 'at'.

triggers.grounds: The band is not over-stated and no cap applies (a single-verse span, so the whole-chapter medium_low cap is not in play), and both edges are byte-clean: 7:18 closes on prohibition plus grounding clause, אַל תַּנַּ֣ח ... כִּֽי יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים (oshb:Eccl.7.18, byte tier), against 7:19's third-person maxim הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תָּעֹ֣ז לֶחָכָ֑ם (oshb:Eccl.7.19, byte tier), and 7:20 opens a fresh maxim כִּ֣י אָדָ֔ם (oshb:Eccl.7.20, byte tier). But the band fails the lane's other two tests. First, no field in the row states any reason for holding at medium_low. Second, the warrant that licenses the row's unit_type deviation is byte-false: the row twice asserts that web:Eccl.7.19 'falls one verse outside' the zone bound at web:Eccl.7.14 when it falls five verses outside it. Two matching findings are recorded; the confidence label itself is defensible, the reasoning offered for it is not.

findings.claim: The row twice states that web:Eccl.7.19 falls 'one verse outside' the sentence-literature zone's bound at web:Eccl.7.14; it falls five verses outside it.
findings.grounds: The book's ruled sentence-literature zone in this chapter is 7:1-14, and ch 7 is identity (WEB 7:1-14 = MT 7:1-14), so no crosswalk question arises. web:Eccl.7.19 stands five verses past the zone's closing verse; the first verse outside the zone is web:Eccl.7.15, which the audited row at that verse itself treats as already reverted to the monologue register. The false distance is repeated in boundary_rationale ('though it falls one verse outside that zone's own bound at web:Eccl.7.14') and in device_notes ('single_saying is applied one verse outside this chapter's own designated sentence zone, which ends at web:Eccl.7.14'), and it is the proximity premise for the paired claim that the verse is 'of the same form as the sentence-zone sayings just before it' -- the sayings immediately before it (web:Eccl.7.16-Eccl.7.18) are the moderation admonition, not sentence-zone sayings, so that clause is unsupported once the distance is corrected. Not load-bearing on either seam (both rest on the register shifts named above); load-bearing on the unit_type deviation licence, which is what the row uses it for.
findings.proposed_change: Correct the distance in both fields (web:Eccl.7.19 stands five verses past the zone's closing verse at web:Eccl.7.14), re-argue the single_saying deviation from the verse's own self-contained comparative construction alone rather than from proximity to the zone, and drop or re-anchor 'the same form as the sentence-zone sayings just before it'. unit_type, confidence and observed_substrate_signals re-open with the driver, per the dependent-field rule.

findings.claim: No field in the row states why the confidence is medium_low.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative, device_notes and observed_substrate_signals all argue the unit_type deviation; none names an uncertainty, and the deviation disclosure asserts the classification rather than doubting it. The book's low-confidence plan requires bespoke uncertainty text on every medium_low/low decision, and the slice's other low-band rows comply: web:Eccl.7.26-Eccl.7.29 ('Held at low confidence honestly rather than resolved: the grammatical gender mismatch at oshb:Eccl.7.27 is a live crux'), web:Eccl.9.13-Eccl.9.16 ('held at medium_low because the v.16/17 seam is genuinely arguable rather than sharply marked'), web:Eccl.10.10-Eccl.10.11 ('Held at medium_low: the K/Q at v.10 complicates the blunt-ax clause's exact sense'). Related and not separately scored: the boundary_rationale absolute 'It shares no content token with the moderation counsel before it or the universal-sinfulness maxim after it' never names its count object. Re-swept word-bound at skeleton tier it is TRUE -- the only token web:Eccl.7.19 shares with oshb:Eccl.7.16-Eccl.7.18 or with oshb:Eccl.7.20 is the relative particle אֲשֶׁ֥ר -- but the row's own rejected_alternative discloses a chokhmah-root echo with oshb:Eccl.7.16's תִּתְחַכַּ֖ם, and the two statements reconcile only through a token-vs-root distinction the row leaves implicit.
findings.proposed_change: Add one bespoke sentence to device_notes naming the actual uncertainty -- a form-based single_saying deviation five verses outside the zone, with the chokhmah-root chain running oshb:Eccl.7.16 -> oshb:Eccl.7.19 -> oshb:Eccl.7.23 / oshb:Eccl.7.25 as the live merge pressure -- and name the count object (word-bound token, not root) on the 'no content token' absolute.

triggers.grounds: Well-calibrated and honestly held. The book's low-confidence plan names 7:26-29 as an expected low region (the amar-qohelet intrusion at 7:27 with the feminine form, plus the one-among-a-thousand crux), and the row's uncertainty text is bespoke to exactly those two grounds rather than boilerplate. The band is not masking a byte-defective warrant. The front seam rests on the participle וּמוֹצֶ֨א אֲנִ֜י (oshb:Eccl.7.26, byte tier) against the perfect search verbs of 7:23-7:25, which the neighbour row argues from the same bytes. The cohesion digit re-derives exactly: matsa tokens across oshb:Eccl.7.27-Eccl.7.29 are 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 over 3 verses -- five perfects (מָצָ֔אתִי at 7:27; מָצָ֑אתִי, מָצָ֔אתִי, מָצָֽאתִי at 7:28; מָצָ֔אתִי at 7:29) plus the infinitive לִמְצֹ֥א at 7:27 -- and every one of the six collates at BYTE tier at its own cited ref. The frame digit is right (amar-qohelet at 3 sites book-wide: 1:2, 7:27, 12:8) and the feminine אָמְרָ֖ה at oshb:Eccl.7.27 is a byte fact, disclosed and left unadjudicated as the book's law allows. Two tier-labelling findings are recorded; neither touches the confidence question. Observation, not scored: frontier_flag_considered is false here, on the slice's only 'low' row, but it is false on all 17 rows visible in this slice including high-confidence ones, so it reads as a uniform schema value rather than a row-level judgment, and the sidecars themselves are outside my assigned paths.

findings.claim: Five fully pointed matsa perfects are quoted under the tier label 'skeleton tier'; all five re-collate at byte tier at their own cited refs.
findings.grounds: The parenthetical reads 'five perfect-tense matsa tokens (skeleton tier, oshb:Eccl.7.27-Eccl.7.29: ...)' and is the only tier label adjacent to those five pointed runs. Collated against their cited refs, מָצָ֔אתִי at oshb:Eccl.7.27, מָצָ֑אתִי / מָצָ֔אתִי / מָצָֽאתִי at oshb:Eccl.7.28 and מָצָ֔אתִי at oshb:Eccl.7.29 all return BYTE tier -- as does לִמְצֹ֥א at oshb:Eccl.7.27, which the row does label byte, so the field is internally inconsistent as well. The splices themselves are sound (the packet normalizer reports 0 defects over this row) and the label understates rather than overstates, so nothing is overclaimed; but it mis-names the collate truth for pointed quotation and leaves ambiguous whether 'skeleton tier' describes the quotations or the root sweep that located them.
findings.proposed_change: Re-label the parenthetical 'byte tier' for the five quoted perfects; or, if 'skeleton tier' was meant to describe the root sweep rather than the quotations, say so explicitly ('root located at skeleton tier; the tokens below are byte tier at their own refs').

findings.claim: 'Both using the identical masculine verb form ... only the qohelet-noun spelling varies between them' holds at accent-stripped tier only; the two quoted verbs differ at byte tier.
findings.grounds: אָמַ֣ר spliced from oshb:Eccl.1.2 collates at BYTE tier at 1:2 but only at ACCENT_STRIPPED tier at oshb:Eccl.12.8, whose own run is אָמַ֥ר -- consonants and vowels match, the accent does not. The identity claim carries no tier, and the rider 'only the qohelet-noun spelling varies between them' is therefore byte-false as written, since the verb accent varies too. The noun half is correct and well-evidenced: קֹהֶ֔לֶת spliced from oshb:Eccl.1.2 returns NONE at oshb:Eccl.12.8, whose own form is the plene definite הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת. The claim is contrastive support for the feminine-form crux at oshb:Eccl.7.27, not a seam warrant, so nothing structural moves.
findings.proposed_change: Name the tier: 'both carry the same masculine form at accent-stripped tier (אָמַ֣ר at oshb:Eccl.1.2, אָמַ֥ר at oshb:Eccl.12.8 -- the accents differ), while the qohelet noun varies in spelling'.

triggers.grounds: Three positional row references stand in row prose, in breach of the register law that row prose describes the text and cross-row references are verse-anchored: 'sets up the specific case the next row develops' (boundary_rationale); 'recurs from the preceding row's own oshb:Eccl.8.3' and 'mirroring that row's own forward disclosure of the same tie' (device_notes). E-18 arm applied -- each embedded claim re-derives TRUE from bytes, so this is register bleed and not an evidence defect: the davar-ra collocation is byte-present at both sites (דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע at oshb:Eccl.8.5 and בְּדָבָ֣ר רָ֑ע at oshb:Eccl.8.3, both BYTE tier); the following unit at web:Eccl.8.10-Eccl.8.14 does develop the specific case this row's close sets up; and the preceding unit at web:Eccl.8.2-Eccl.8.4 does carry the mirrored forward disclosure. The third instance is the worst of the three because it describes another row's disclosure practice rather than the text. The row is otherwise byte-solid -- its headline directional tier claim verifies exactly, re-collated in the second finding's grounds -- so the defect is cosmetic. Matching finding recorded at low.

findings.claim: Three positional row references stand in the row's prose where the verse anchors already carry the same content.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'sets up the specific case the next row develops'. device_notes: 'recurs from the preceding row's own oshb:Eccl.8.3' and 'mirroring that row's own forward disclosure of the same tie'. All three are barred by the register purge, and all three point at verses already anchored (oshb:Eccl.8.3 explicitly; web:Eccl.8.10 through boundary_evidence_refs). Every underlying claim re-derives true from bytes, so no evidence is affected: דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.8.5, byte tier) and בְּדָבָ֣ר רָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.8.3, byte tier) are the two davar-ra sites, and the neighbour row at web:Eccl.8.2-Eccl.8.4 does disclose the same pair forward.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale: 'which both caps this reflection and sets up the specific case taken up at web:Eccl.8.10'. device_notes: 'recurs from oshb:Eccl.8.3', and delete the clause 'mirroring that row's own forward disclosure of the same tie' outright, since the tie is disclosed at both ends already. Pair rule: the mirrored clause in the neighbour row at web:Eccl.8.2-Eccl.8.4 ('at the following row's own opening cluster') takes the same cut in one edit.

findings.claim: device_notes says the davar-ra collocation 'opens this row's own opening verse' at oshb:Eccl.8.5; it stands mid-verse, not at the verse opening.
findings.grounds: MT 8:5 opens שׁוֹמֵ֣ר מִצְוָ֔ה (byte tier at oshb:Eccl.8.5); דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע (byte tier at oshb:Eccl.8.5) is the fifth and sixth words, standing at the atnach that divides the verse. The collocation is byte-present as claimed and the tie to oshb:Eccl.8.3 is real, so only the position word is wrong -- and the neighbour row states the same tie without the error ('at the following row's own opening cluster'). Mechanical; nothing rests on it. Related looseness in the same row, not separately scored: boundary_rationale introduces 'A gnomic principle opens this reflection' with a splice of 8:5's SECOND half, וְעֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֔ט יֵדַ֖ע לֵ֥ב חָכָֽם (oshb:Eccl.8.5, byte tier) -- defensible as opening the reflection, i.e. the span, but it is not the verse's opening clause either. For the record the row's central tier claim is exact and survives re-collation: עֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט spliced from oshb:Eccl.8.6 returns BYTE at 8:6 and ACCENT_STRIPPED at oshb:Eccl.8.5, while וְעֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֔ט spliced from oshb:Eccl.8.5 returns NONE at oshb:Eccl.8.6 -- exactly the asymmetric containment the row asserts.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'that opens this row's own opening verse, oshb:Eccl.8.5' with 'that stands in this row's own opening verse, oshb:Eccl.8.5'.

triggers.grounds: Well-calibrated, and every digit re-derives. The stated reason for the band is bespoke and honest ('held at medium_low because the v.16/17 seam is genuinely arguable rather than sharply marked'), and the row discloses its counter-evidence in full rather than suppressing it. Re-derived from bytes: the catchword occupies exactly 2 verses book-wide (MT 9:16, 9:17), so 'book-unique ... (sweep: 2 verses book-wide)' is true with object and digit named, and both runs are byte-present (נִשְׁמָעִֽים at oshb:Eccl.9.16, נִשְׁמָעִ֑ים at oshb:Eccl.9.17); the davar root does bridge the seam (וּדְבָרָ֖יו at oshb:Eccl.9.16, דִּבְרֵ֣י at oshb:Eccl.9.17, both byte tier); and the 'byte-identical two-word frame' claim survives at the tier it names -- טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה spliced from oshb:Eccl.9.16 collates at BYTE tier at oshb:Eccl.9.18 AND at oshb:Eccl.7.11, and a skeleton sweep of the pair returns exactly those 3 verses, so the tier word is earned rather than an overclaim. The seam warrant is the ruled sentence-literature zone opening at 9:17 plus the genitive-headed דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֔ים (oshb:Eccl.9.17, byte tier), handled correctly under the book's header-vs-genitive hazard (only 1:1 is a header, and the row says so). No tier-4 fact appears anywhere in the row, and no mark inside the span goes undisclosed. Observation, not scored: the neighbour row at web:Eccl.9.17 grades the SAME seam 'high' while disclosing the same catchword counter-signal; because both sides argue the seam identically this is a confidence asymmetry rather than an incompatibly argued seam, and this row's disclosure-rich medium_low is the defensible side of it.

Well-calibrated and unusually well-evidenced for a low band. The book's low-confidence plan names 'saying_cluster rows whose cohesion evidence is thinner than 2 shared content tokens' as an expected low region, and the row's stated reason is exactly that plus the K/Q at v.10 -- bespoke, not boilerplate. Both named cohesion drivers re-derive true with their count objects correctly named. The yitron family occupies 9 verses book-wide (MT 1:3, 2:11, 2:13, 3:9, 5:8, 5:15, 7:12, 10:10, 10:11 -- six bare and three vav-prefixed), and MT 10:10 / 10:11 is the only consecutive-verse pair among them. Verse-initial אִם occupies exactly 6 verses (MT 5:7, 6:3, 10:4, 10:10, 10:11, 11:3), 3 of them in ch 10, and 10:10 / 10:11 is again the only consecutive pair; neither oshb:Eccl.10.9 (opens מַסִּ֣יעַ) nor oshb:Eccl.10.12 (opens דִּבְרֵ֥י) opens on it. The one-directional tier claim is exact: יִתְר֔וֹן spliced from oshb:Eccl.10.11 returns BYTE at 10:11 and only ACCENT_STRIPPED at oshb:Eccl.10.10, while וְיִתְר֥וֹן spliced from oshb:Eccl.10.10 returns NONE at oshb:Eccl.10.11. The K/Q is correctly disclosed and correctly spliced -- MT 10:10 is in the ketiv/qere inventory, and the row's run הכשיר הַכְשֵׁ֖ר reproduces the inline unpointed ketiv ahead of its pointed qere at BYTE tier, which is the book's hardest slicing hazard handled right. No mark inside the span goes undisclosed. Two low findings are recorded; neither touches the confidence question.

findings.claim: The splice יִתְר֔וֹן at oshb:Eccl.10.11 is glossed 'and there is no advantage' -- a gloss whose extent covers the preceding וְאֵ֣ין, which is not inside the splice.
findings.grounds: MT 10:11's own bytes run וְאֵ֣ין יִתְר֔וֹן לְבַ֖עַל הַלָּשֽׁוֹן (byte tier at oshb:Eccl.10.11). The row splices only יִתְר֔וֹן ('advantage') and glosses it 'and there is no advantage', which renders וְאֵ֣ין יִתְר֔וֹן. The substantive claim the gloss supports -- that the keyword stands negated here against its affirmed form at 10:10 -- is true, and the sibling splice at oshb:Eccl.10.10 is parity-correct (וְיִתְר֥וֹן glossed 'and the advantage of'). Quote/gloss extent mismatch only; the cohesion driver is unaffected.
findings.proposed_change: Either extend the splice to וְאֵ֣ין יִתְר֔וֹן (oshb:Eccl.10.11, byte tier) to match the gloss, or cut the gloss back to 'advantage' and carry the negation as prose ('negated by the preceding וְאֵ֣ין').

findings.claim: device_notes carries a positional row reference where the verse anchor already carries the tie.
findings.grounds: device_notes reads 'הַנָּחָ֖שׁ (oshb:Eccl.10.11) here and נָחָֽשׁ (oshb:Eccl.10.8) in the preceding row' -- the verse is named, so the positional row reference adds nothing, and the register law bars it. The claim itself re-derives true: a skeleton sweep of the noun returns exactly 2 verses book-wide (MT 10:8, 10:11), matching the row's digit, and both bite-root verbs are byte-present (יִשֹּׁ֥ךְ at oshb:Eccl.10.11, יִשְּׁכֶ֥נּוּ at oshb:Eccl.10.8). Cosmetic register bleed only.
findings.proposed_change: Delete 'in the preceding row' -- 'הַנָּחָ֖שׁ (oshb:Eccl.10.11) here and נָחָֽשׁ (oshb:Eccl.10.8)' already carries the tie. Pair rule: the mirrored clause in the neighbour unit at web:Eccl.10.8-Eccl.10.9 ('in the row that follows') takes the same cut in the same edit.
